Using AWS CloudTrail, a user in a management account can\\ncreate an organization trail that logs all events for all AWS accounts in that\\norganization. Organization trails are automatically applied to all member accounts in the\\norganization. Member accounts can see the organization trail, but can't modify or delete it.\\nBy default, member accounts don't have access to the log files for the organization trail in\\nthe Amazon S3 bucket. This helps you uniformly apply and enforce your event logging strategy\\nacross the accounts in your organization.\\n\\nFor more information, see Creating a Trail for an Organization in the\\n*AWS CloudTrail User Guide*.\\n\\nUse the following information to help you integrate\\nAWS CloudTrail with AWS Organizations\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/services-that-can-integrate-cloudtrail.html\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"Creating a trail for an organization\",\"context\":\"# Creating a trail for an organization\\n\\nIf you have created an organization in AWS Organizations, you can create a trail that logs all\\nevents for all AWS accounts in that organization. The default is false, and cannot be true unless the call is made on behalf of an Amazon Web Services account that is the management account for an organization in Organizations. If the trail is not an organization trail and this is set to `true`, the trail will be created in all Amazon Web Services accounts that belong to the organization. {"id": "0a78c3f9-7efb-417e-a358-038da62fe554", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "tool_summary", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "tooluse_b90aKrfzF4ndcliO4prTSQ", "status": "success", "content": [{"text": "{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"status\":\"SUCCESS\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/view-cloudtrail-events.html\",\"content\":\"# Working with CloudTrail event history\\n\\nCloudTrail is enabled by default for your AWS account and you automatically have access to the CloudTrail event history.\\nThe event history provides a viewable, searchable, downloadable, and immutable record of the past 90 days of management events\\nin an AWS Region. These events capture activity made through the AWS Management Console, AWS Command Line Interface, and AWS SDKs\\nand APIs. The event history records events in the AWS Region where the event happened. There are no CloudTrail charges for viewing the event history.\\n\\nYou can look up events related to the creation, modification, or deletion of resources\\n(such as IAM users or Amazon EC2 instances) in your AWS account on a by-Region basis on the CloudTrail console\\nby viewing the **Event history** page. You can also look up these events by running the `aws cloudtrail\\nlookup-events` command or by using the `LookupEvents` API.\\n\\nYou can use the **Event history** page on the CloudTrail console to view,\\nsearch, download, archive, analyze, and respond to account activity across your AWS\\ninfrastructure. You can customize the\\nview of the **Event history** page on the console by selecting\\nhow many events to display on each page and which columns to display or hide. You can also\\ncompare the details of events in event history side-by-side. You can programmatically look up events by using the AWS SDKs or\\nAWS Command Line Interface.\\n\\n**Note:**\\n\\nOver time, AWS services might add additional events. CloudTrail records these events in\\nevent history, but a full 90-day record of activity that\\nincludes added events won't be available until 90 days after it adds the events.\\n\\nThe event history is separate from any trails or event data\\nstores that you create for your account. Changes you make to your event data stores or\\ntrails do not affect the event history.\\n\\nThe sections which follow describe how to look up recent management events by using the CloudTrail console and the AWS CLI, and\\ndescribe how to download a file of events. For information about using the\\n`LookupEvents` API to retrieve information from CloudTrail events, see LookupEvents\\nin the *AWS CloudTrail API Reference*.\\n\\n**Topics**\\n\\n* Limitations of Event history\\n* Viewing recent management events with the console\\n* Viewing recent management events with the AWS CLI\\n\\n## Limitations of Event history\\n\\nThe following limitations apply to the event history.\\n\\n* The **Event history** page on the CloudTrail console only shows management events. It does not show data events, Insights events, or network activity events.\\n* The event history is limited to the past 90 days of events. For an ongoing record of events in your AWS account, create an event data store or a trail.\\n* When you download events from the **Event history** page on\\n  the CloudTrail console, you can download up to 200,000 events in a single file. If you reach the 200,000 event limit,\\n  the CloudTrail console will provide the option to download additional files.\\n* The event history doesn't provide organization level event aggregation. To record events across your organization, create an organization event data store or trail.\\n* An event history search is limited to a single AWS account, only returns events from a single AWS Region, and cannot query multiple attributes.\\n  You can only apply one attribute filter and a time range filter.\\n\\n  You can create a CloudTrail Lake event data store to query across multiple attributes and AWS Regions. You can also query across multiple AWS accounts in an AWS Organizations organization.\\n  In CloudTrail Lake, you can query multiple event types, including management events, data events, Insights events, AWS Config\\n  configuration items, Audit Manager evidence, and non-AWS events. CloudTrail Lake queries offer a deeper and more\\n  customizable view of events than simple key and value lookups on the **Event\\n  history** page, or by running `LookupEvents`. For more information,\\n  see Working with AWS CloudTrail Lake and Create an event data store for CloudTrail events with the console.\\n* You cannot exclude AWS KMS or Amazon RDS Data API events from event history; settings that you apply to a trail or event data store do not apply to event history.\",\"total_length\":4239,\"start_index\":0,\"end_index\":4239,\"truncated\":false,\"redirected_url\":null,\"error_code\":null}]}}"}]}], "label": "Read CloudTrail Event history documentation"}

{"id": "198ae50c-6b65-42aa-a3e3-1a08a03dedc6", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "**Short answer:** Your auditors shouldn't rely on Event history alone. It only covers 90 days of management events, one Region at a time. Your organization trail is also something you can see but can't read or control from this account.

## Your trails

| Trail | Scope | What it records |
|---|---|---|
| `example-org-trail` (organization trail, owned by account 111122223333, home Region us-east-2) | Multi-Region, global service events included | Custom event selectors are set. I can't read them from a member account, so I can't confirm what it captures. |
| `account-baseline-trail` | Multi-Region, global service events included, log file validation on | Default selectors, so management events only |
| `nebula-single-region-trail` | us-east-1 only, no global service events, validation off | Default selectors, so management events only |
| `nebula-data-events-trail` | us-east-1 only, validation off | Only S3 object data events for `nebula-audit-covered-012345678901/`. It has no management events. |

All the local trails were delivering logs when I checked. I confirmed this directly for `nebula-single-region-trail`, which delivered as recently as 15:34 UTC today.

## What the organization trail covers

- **Applied automatically.** An organization trail is applied to every member account, including this one. Member accounts can see it but can't modify or delete it.
- **No log access by default.** The logs go to an S3 bucket (`sample-bucket-01`) in the management account. Members don't get access to those logs unless someone grants it.
- **Scope is unverified.** I couldn't read the organization trail's event selectors from here. Someone with access to the management account needs to confirm whether it logs management events, data events, or both.

## Why Event history isn't enough for auditors

- It covers only the **past 90 days** of events.
- It shows **management events only**. It has no data events, Insights events, or network activity events.
- Each search covers **one account and one Region**, with a single attribute filter plus a time range.
- It doesn't aggregate events across the organization.
- It is separate from trails. Nothing you configure on a trail changes it.

AWS's own guidance is to create a trail or event data store for an ongoing record. Event history is a convenience for recent lookups, not an audit record.

## Gaps to raise with your auditors

1. **Data events** are only captured for one S3 bucket, in us-east-1. Any other bucket, Lambda, or DynamoDB data activity isn't recorded by your local trails. The organization trail might cover it, but that's unconfirmed.
2. **Log file validation is off** on both `nebula-*` trails. Auditors usually want it on for integrity evidence. The sandbox trail has it on.
3. **Retention and access.** Your auditors can't use the organization trail's logs unless the management account gives them access. Your local trails write to bucket `nebula-ct-gap-012345678901`, and the sandbox trail writes to its own bucket in this account. Check that those buckets' retention and lifecycle settings meet your audit period.

The management account owner can confirm the organization trail's selectors and set up cross-account log access. I can also check the S3 bucket retention settings on your local trails if you'd like.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
